Analysis: Hypothesis 1 builds on established signaling through androgen receptor and glycolytic enzyme HK2, linking them to an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and drug resistance. While it provides a multifaceted therapeutic strategy and includes compensatory pathway monitoring, its integration of multiple advanced modalities (CRISPR/Cas9, RNA interference) raises concerns around mechanistic proof and clinical feasibility. Hypothesis 2, on the other hand, introduces a novel angle by targeting a circular RNA (circMAT2B) to influence PKM2 activity and metabolic reprogramming. This approach is more focused and relies on measurable metabolic endpoints such as lactate production and HIF-1α stabilization, making it comparatively more testable. Although both hypotheses would benefit from strengthened mechanistic validation, hypothesis 2 is more novel and has a clearer experimental setup that could potentially offer a safer, streamlined intervention strategy.
